Drop goes live: Friday 3 October, 10:00am PT. Dates always move, so keep this editable.

1. Ember Mug. Wheel-thrown, glazed in rust. $42.
2. Sprig Bowl. My everyday bowl, back in green. $38.

This one is the whole reason I do a coffee-bar collab every autumn: I wanted a pour-over set that feels like the studio it came out of, so I threw the dripper and the mug as one piece, fired them together, and glazed them in the same kiln-clay batch so they read as a pair on the shelf and on your counter, and the coffee is by the people I actually buy my own beans from - In collaboration with Fernhollow Coffee. 7. Warm Ground Vase. $72.
8. A note on the glazes this drop: everything you see is the real fired colour, shot next to my test tiles so nothing drifts, because the glaze is the whole product and I would rather you get exactly the tan and the rust and the green that turns up at your door than a prettier photo of a colour that does not exist - if a frame could not be brought to the true colour I cut it, and I would rather post fewer honest pictures than a feed that lies about the clay.
9. Kiln Clay Serving Platter. The big one. $88.

assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the printer's existing piece-card press PDF (flat, single record; to be reverse-engineered downstream).

Document: single piece card, 70 x 100 mm PORTRAIT, NO bleed box present (trim = media box, 0 mm bleed), fonts embedded. This is the card the printer already runs a batch of, one per piece, to go in the shipping box and stand on the market stall.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (reads as tidy separate fields):
- Top: a square PIECE PHOTO, roughly 58 x 58 mm, matted on the Warm Ground colour.
- Under it: the PIECE NAME in the warm humanist serif, large.
- Under it: a GLAZE line in a small sans (e.g. 'Kiln Clay glaze'), with a small round GLAZE DOT printed beside it in that glaze's own colour.
- Under it: the PRICE in the serif.
- Bottom: a fixed footer line, 'Hand-thrown in a shared studio in Portland by Marlo Quill', and beneath it room for the collaboration credit where a piece carries one.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The PIECE NAME, the GLAZE line and the PRICE are a SINGLE continuous text story in ONE text frame flowing top to bottom, NOT three addressable frames, so every field offset must be computed from the document's own reconstructed story text.
- The square PIECE PHOTO at the top IS a real rectangular graphic frame, the ONLY one on the card, so each piece's own picture binds here.
- The round GLAZE DOT is a DECORATIVE grouped vector path in the glaze colour, NOT a second picture/graphic frame, even though it reads like a per-glaze swatch well; there is nothing to bind into it.
- The fixed maker line and the collaboration credit are a SEPARATE short story. The credit sits at the TAIL of that story, so an offset computed from the shortened mapping readout (which collapses the long fixed maker line) lands short of it and silently drops the credit on the one card that carries one.
- So the frame inventory a conversion exposes (roughly: one flowing name/glaze/price story + one square graphic frame + one decorative dot path + one footer story) is nothing like the tidy fields the printed card suggests, and there is exactly one graphic frame to bind a picture into.

NO BLEED: because the media box equals the trim and no bleed box exists, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured from this file however the render is called.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): PIECE_NAME | GLAZE | PRICE | PIECE_PHOTO | COLLAB_CREDIT

Colours: Warm Ground #E7D9C4 photo mat and ground, Bench Ink #33291F piece name and price, Sprig Green #6E7A4E footer text, glaze dot printed in the named glaze's own palette colour.
